findings: Library, not paper: all seven forms of the target now have a timelike-line witness (kb/0011). The extra _noArc m-GHD form has one too. Each witness states the form's hypotheses on concrete data, or takes them from one data theorem (mughdData), and states the form's conclusion on that data. Its proof term applies the form itself, not the original (Probe.lean USES lines).

Library, not paper: the planner's sketch for the union lemmas (B = ⊤, 𝒟 = {⊤}, S = {0}) is trivial for two of them. With S a singleton, eq_of_mem's conclusion c s = c t follows from c s, c t ∈ S alone. of_subset can then only take S' = S (S' = ∅ is Cauchy only in an open set with no inextensible curve). So the witnesses use B = ]-1, 1[ ∪ ]2, 4[ and S = {0, 3}, which is Cauchy in B and acausal there. No connected open set of the line containing both points has it as a Cauchy surface: the identity curve would meet it twice. 𝒟 is the infinite family of intervals ]a - r, a + r[ with a ∈ S and 0 < r < 1/2. Its union is not a member, and its pieces have different Cauchy surfaces, {0} and {3}.

Library, not paper: the 4.79/4.80 hypotheses hold for the problem whose solutions are the restrictions of id to every open set of the line, not only for the one-domain problem of timelikeLine_ers_theorem_4_79_4_80 (sol U u := U = ⊤ ∧ …). The reason: a development of {0} is preconnected (isPreconnected_of_isCauchySurfaceOn_of_t1_secondCountable), and two developments meet in a common development (kb/0245). So Cor 4.73's named inputs hlocal, hstay and hstep (local_uniqueness, frontier_stays_in, slice_restart) are theorems for every pair of developments of this problem. hG, hT and hK hold on every open set of the line: GH by timelikeLine_globallyHyperbolicOn, tarentin by the new ErsSCWitness.tarentinOn, compact slabs by compactSlabs_singleton.

Library, not paper: Causal.Ers464WithoutArc's SCOPE says 'Cor 4.68 and the m-GHD form have no witness'. The m-GHD half is now stale: timelikeLine_isUniqueDevelopment_secondCountable_noArc is a witness for IsMDevelopment.isUniqueDevelopment_secondCountable_noArc. Editing that docstring is the loop's job, not done here. Cor 4.68 is T-abs-ers-witnesses'.

Limitation, disclosed in SCOPE: every witness uses one causality, cau u = Cm = timelikeLine. None separates the PDE's causality from Minkowski's, so hsub and hinext hold by refl. The cheap separating candidate on ℝ fails. Take cau u the spacelike line inside Cm the timelike line. Its causal curves are constant and cannot strictly extend (the image cannot grow). So every constant curve is inextensible for it, which breaks hinext, and {0} is Cauchy in no open set. This is argued, not proved in Lean.
questions: The configuration of the union witnesses. The target's sketch was B = ⊤, 𝒟 = {⊤}, S = {0}. The evidence asked for non-trivial witnesses 'where possible', so I took B = ]-1, 1[ ∪ ]2, 4[, S = {0, 3} and 𝒟 infinite. The singleton instance is not stated separately. If the loop wants it too, it is four one-line applications of the same forms to timelikeLine_globallyHyperbolic, timelikeLine_causallyArcConnected and timelikeLine_isCauchySurface_zero.

eq_of_mem's 'conclusion on that data'. Every inhabitant of its hypotheses has c s = c t, which is what the lemma says. On the inhabitant (the constant curve 0, s = 0 ≠ t = 1), that conclusion is 0 = 0. I also stated the conclusion for every causal curve of every W ≤ B, with S having two points, and took that as meeting kb/0011. This is a reading of the witness rule, not of the paper.
kb_proposals: A non-trivial witness for the ERS union lemmas on the line: S = {0, 3} is Cauchy in ]-1, 1[ ∪ ]2, 4[ (Causal.ErsSCWitness.isCauchySurfaceOn_twoIntervals), proved by isCauchySurfaceOn_sSup_of_isAcausalOn with the union itself as ambient. The infinite family ErsSCWitness.pieces, whose union is not a member, serves all four second countable union lemmas. {a} is Cauchy in ]a - r, a + r[ by ErsSCWitness.isCauchySurfaceOn_Ioo_center (T-abs-ers-sc-witnesses).

On the timelike line, for the problem whose solutions are id on every open set (ErsSCWitness.idSol, S = {0}), every development is preconnected. Two developments meet in the common development U₁ ⊓ U₂. Cor 4.73's hlocal, hstay and hstep hold for every pair (isCommonDevelopment_inf, frontierStaysIn, sliceRestart; ErsSCWitness.mughdData). This gives a witness for 4.73, 4.79, 4.80 and the m-GHD forms with every open interval around 0 as a development domain, not one domain (T-abs-ers-sc-witnesses).

The timelike line is GH on every open set (timelikeLine_globallyHyperbolicOn, Causal.CBG.CausalConvex). It is tarentin on every open set (Causal.ErsSCWitness.tarentinOn; twin Causal.timelikeLine_tarentinOn in T-abs-ers-witnesses' file) and has compact slabs over a point (GloballyHyperbolicOn.compactSlabs_singleton). So hG, hT and hK of ERS §4 hold on every open set of the line.
